# Outpatient registration (his-backend `encounter` GraphQL + REST, his-frontend encounter form)

**Goal:** a registration officer can register an outpatient visit once, with the right payor, poli,
doctor and time slot — and the encounter that comes out of it is complete, traceable and not
readable or writable by anyone who cannot prove a session.

**Docs:** test doc [outpatient-registration-testing.md](../../outpatient-registration-testing.md) · module features: [module catalogue](../../modules/README.md) (linked on every story).

Epic code `OUTREG`. Source of the stories and findings:
`his-v3-ai/services-impl/202611/backend-rest-e2e-qa-assessment/data-integration/D-HISV3-OUTPATIENT-REGISTRATION/`
(`USER-STORIES.md` → `US-D-HISV3-OUTPATIENT-REGISTRATION-01..20`, `USER-SCENARIOS.md` →
`SC-D-HISV3-OUTPATIENT-REGISTRATION-01..06`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` §6 → findings `OR-01..OR-22`).

The story ids of this catalog are short (`US-OUTREG-NN`); the mapping is one to one:
`US-OUTREG-01` = `US-D-HISV3-OUTPATIENT-REGISTRATION-01`, and so on.

## User stories

- **US-OUTREG-01** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07)) — As a registration officer I want to create an outpatient visit for a registered patient so that the patient can be treated in the chosen poli.
- **US-OUTREG-02** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07)) — As a registration officer I want to pick the right payor and coverage so that the visit is billed correctly.
- **US-OUTREG-03** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07)) — As a registration officer I want to pick the poli, the doctor and the time slot so that the visit is scheduled where it belongs.
- **US-OUTREG-04** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07)) — As a registration officer I want a warning when the patient already has an active outpatient visit so that no visit and no bill is duplicated.
- **US-OUTREG-05** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07), [A02.01](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a02-01)) — As a poli officer I want a registration number at check-in so that the queue is unambiguous.
- **US-OUTREG-06** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07)) — As a registration officer I want the outpatient visit to carry a registration number from the start so that reports, billing and the transformer feed are complete.
- **US-OUTREG-07** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07), [A02.01](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a02-01)) — As a poli officer I want the queue to show a unique number and a barcode so that every patient is called unambiguously.
- **US-OUTREG-08** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07)) — As a registration officer I want to give the patient a printable proof of registration so that the patient has a document of the visit.
- **US-OUTREG-09** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07)) — As an IT officer I want every surface that writes an outpatient encounter to be authenticated so that patient data cannot be written or read by an unauthorized caller.
- **US-OUTREG-10** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07)) — As a registration officer I want an actionable error message so that I know what to correct.
- **US-OUTREG-11** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07), [D09.01](../../modules/D-corporate.md#f-d09-01)) — As a data manager I want the outpatient visit to carry a registration number since it is created so that the transformer feed `regpas` is complete.
- **US-OUTREG-12** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07)) — As a registration officer I want the registration number to be free of race conditions so that two patients never share one.
- **US-OUTREG-13** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07)) — As a registration officer I want one active outpatient visit per patient so that no bill is duplicated.
- **US-OUTREG-14** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07), [A02.01](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a02-01)) — As a poli officer I want the barcode check-in to produce a correct registration number so that the barcode can be used as the check-in identity.
- **US-OUTREG-15** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07)) — As an IT officer I want the REST encounter surface to be authenticated so that no encounter and no bill can be created by an integrator without a session.
- **US-OUTREG-16** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07), [A02.01](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a02-01)) — As a poli officer I want the queue number to be free of collisions so that two patients are never called with the same number.
- **US-OUTREG-17** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07)) — As a registration officer I want an honest failure report so that I do not repeat a registration that already succeeded.
- **US-OUTREG-18** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07)) — As a registration officer I want the poli, the doctor and the slot to stay mandatory so that the visit cannot be saved half-filled.
- **US-OUTREG-19** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07)) — As a registration officer I want the patient data to be stored consistently so that the downstream services read the same values.
- **US-OUTREG-20** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07)) — As an auditor I want the encounter write to carry the identity of the caller so that every change is traceable.

## Defect ids

The findings of the cluster documentation keep their `OR-nn` number and get a defect id of this
suite: `DEF-850` = OR-01, `DEF-851` = OR-02, … `DEF-871` = OR-22 (the number is `849` + the finding
number). The rows that pin a finding are marked `xfail` in the scenario text; they are automated as
**expected failures** (`test.fail()` + a `defect` annotation), so a fix shows up as an
"unexpectedly passed".

One finding is **not** in the cluster documentation — it came out of the reading of the current
source and got the next free id:

| Defect    | Finding                                                                                              | Evidence                                                                                                                               |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DEF-872` | the barcode check-in never answers — it crashes the request instead of writing a registration number | `GenerateRegistrationNumberByBarcodeCode` ends in `panic("implement me")` (`his-backend/internal/storage/encounter/encounter.go:5685`) |

## Status of this catalog

Written 2026-11-11 from the static reading of `his-backend@staging` (3743680c2),
`his-frontend@bugfix/adjustment-radiology-result-cloud-send-111126` and of the cluster
documentation of `his-v3-ai`.

**No case has been executed yet.** The staging environment of the run machine does not accept the
credentials of `env/.env.staging` (`userLogin` answers "gagal melakukan otentikasi dengan username
dan password yang diberikan"), so every case that needs a session stays `blocked`. That is an
environment fact, not a property of the specs: the same credentials make the pre-existing
`D-HISV3-PATIENT-REGISTRATION` suite fail the same way.

A row is `automated` when its spec exists **and passes**; a row that pins an open defect is
`blocked` with the reason `defect:DEF-nnn`; a row that cannot run yet is `blocked` with the reason
that says why. Nothing is marked `automated` today.
